monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, trading some easy running for more Zone 3–4 work — reflected in faster pace, higher HR, and elevated aerobic TE, though cadence dipped slightly.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved despite a 4 spm drop in cadence — suggesting better cardiovascular economy at given intensities, likely supported by the 27% time spent in Zone 3 this month (up from 31% last month but now paired with faster pace and higher HR).

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.4 more km across 4 sessions in the remaining 15 days to match last month’s 61.0 km — averaging 2.35 km per session, or two 3–4 km runs and two 1.5 km easy runs.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite lower cadence
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose to 13.52 m/sec per bpm (from 13.46), even as average cadence fell from 151 to 147 spm — indicating improved oxygen utilization per heartbeat, possibly due to stronger Zone 3–4 stimulus (27% Z3 + 19% Z4 = 46% combined this month vs 32% last month).

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity distribution
insights.body: Zone 4 time increased to 19% (from 15%) and Zone 5 appeared at 7% (vs 1% last month), while Zone 1 dropped sharply to 14% (from 24%) — signaling reduced recovery volume and greater emphasis on threshold and VO2 max efforts.

insights.title: Stride length compression at longer distances
insights.body: On your 14.1 km run (July 12), stride length dropped to 70.36 cm — 15 cm shorter than your shortest non-long-run (85.27 cm on July 8) — and ground contact increased to 319 ms, suggesting accumulating fatigue or form breakdown beyond ~10 km.

insights.title: Higher aerobic TE without VO2 max increase
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose to 3.0 (from 2.7), yet VO2 max remains stable at 39.0 (except one 40.0 reading on July 15), indicating training effect is currently driving adaptation more than physiological ceiling change — a sign of effective periodization if recovery is managed.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on your next easy day, focusing on cadence ≥150 spm using metronome cues.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 % dropped to 33% (from 29% last month but still below ideal base-building range), and cadence averaged only 147 spm this month — rebuilding rhythm and aerobic foundation will support sustainable Z3/Z4 work.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 2-min strides at 4:45/km pace (475 sec/km) after an easy 4 km run this week, walking 90 sec between.
recommendations.reason: Your best recent pace is 475 sec/km (July 17), and you spent only 7% in Zone 5 — introducing short, controlled neuromuscular efforts will improve turnover without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Perform a 10 km run at 5:30/km (330 sec/km) — targeting avg HR 142–146 bpm — with cadence goal of 152 spm and stride length ≥75 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your longest run was 14.1 km at 9:25/km (565 sec/km) with HR 141 bpm; inserting a moderate-duration, moderately hard run at threshold pace bridges Z3 and Z4 and aligns with your current 519 sec/km avg pace.

weekly_focus.description: Reinforce neuromuscular coordination and fatigue resistance through intentional cadence work, controlled threshold efforts, and strategic recovery — balancing your recent jump in intensity with form-aware volume.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥150 spm)
